Talking about CZ75 SP-01 Shadow i posted last week.

Had to call a BUNCH of ranges to find one that isn't closed for a month, and drive to the next city but i scratched my curiosity itch.

Feels similar to the classic 75B, has that "pirate cannon" feeling with all the heavy steel slapping back and forth in a slow motion. The trigger is a bit nicer than the old B, and waaay nicer and easier to use than any striker fired gun i ever tried. A 50 shot group, offhand slow fire, at 50m looked to be all 50 in a head sized circle. Couldn't really tell due to the oversized shot markers from the projectors, will have to visit a normal range with paper targets, but i was very satisfied for a new gun i don't know yet, and i bet it can do even better.

Was pulling to the left, not sure if it was me or the sights, could be ether since the "length of pull" is a bit small for me, but the factory 25m test group was an inch to the left too, and i doubt they adjusted the sights after that. They do offer "large hands" replacement trigger for 30$ so i will consider that for the future, but not before i bench rest it on another occasion to check if the sights are 100%. Maybe its an inherent disadvantage of the DA/SA, as they have to find a middle ground between to long and the short pull. Single action only will forever be king for target shooting i guess.

But i really like the safety aspect of DA/SA and the fact that i can forget the safety even exists, because this is gonna be my go to defense gun as well. As a matter of fact, with the hammer lowered, the safety can't even be engaged at all, so there is now way to fuck myself over. I like that design detail a lot. There is also a half-cock position if you pull the trigger half way by accident, then back off, it stops before it hits the firing pin (this model has no firing pin block). Also, if i ever end up signing up for IPSC, SA trigger guns aren't permitted in production division anyway. I am a DA/SA technocrat shill prophet.

I had 0 failures of any kind out of the 100 rounds i shot. A small sample, but considering the conditions i believe it's telling. Firstly its a VERY tight fit between the guide rods, they are full length and they obviously haven't been broken in yet. Second, i like to have a very limp wrist when slow firing. Third, i ran 25/100rds of 140grain subsonic. With the deliberate limp wrist, tolerances not broken in yet, and subsonic ammo, all working against the gun at the same time, and it still chambered flawlessly for all 100 rounds.

A CZ user has a choice to treat it like a 1911.
